raw_response:
I’m 64 this year, and after 38 years on this land I don’t like making big changes unless I have a strong reason. My main thing is still wheat-maize on most of the land, because that gives steady grain and spreads risk. Cotton I’ll keep on a small piece, not too much, because it takes more hand work and there are only two people in my house. The well is there, but pumping costs money, so for wheat I’ll protect the key waterings, and for maize and cotton I’ll watch the rain first. The extension people say don’t overdo fertilizer, but from my own fields I know if wheat or maize runs short of nitrogen, yield drops fast, so I’ll still use a solid amount, just not too aggressive because cash is tight.
